subsystems.name: Topical delivery system
subsystems.role: Carries active molecules past the skin's outer barrier to reach living cells.

subsystems.name: Active compounds
subsystems.role: Modify epigenetic marks to restore youthful gene expression.
parts: small-molecule inhibitors of DNA methyltransferases or histone deacetylases
synthetic messenger RNA or small interfering RNA

subsystems.name: Target cells
subsystems.role: The skin cells whose epigenetic state is to be reset.

subsystems.name: Epigenetic machinery
subsystems.role: The enzymes that write, erase and read DNA methylation and histone modifications.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and safety assays
subsystems.role: Measure epigenetic age and detect unwanted cell changes.
parts: DNA methylation arrays or epigenetic clocks

buildSteps.title: Map the aging epigenome in skin
buildSteps.detail: Compare DNA methylation patterns in fibroblasts from young and old donors to identify marks that change with age.

buildSteps.title: Screen reprogramming molecules
buildSteps.detail: Test libraries of small molecules, RNAs or proteins on cultured fibroblasts to find candidates that reverse those marks without killing the cells.

buildSteps.title: Design a topical formulation
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate the active molecules in nanoparticles or liposomes and incorporate them into a cream that can cross the stratum corneum (about 10–20 µm thick) and reach the dermis (1–2 mm deep).

buildSteps.title: Test on human skin models
buildSteps.detail: Apply the formulation to 3D skin equivalents or donated skin explants and measure changes in epigenetic age, collagen production and cell behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Assess safety in animals
buildSteps.detail: Run preclinical studies in mice or pigs to check for skin irritation, systemic exposure and any sign of uncontrolled cell growth or cancer.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Phase I trials test safety in a small group; later trials measure whether wrinkles, elasticity or other signs of aging improve.

buildSteps.title: Scale up and regulate
buildSteps.detail: Manufacture the formulation under pharmaceutical-quality controls and seek approval from drug regulators as a medicine, not a cosmetic.

prerequisites.why: DNA methylation clocks and partial reprogramming with Yamanaka factors are established in cells and animals.

prerequisites.tech: Safe topical delivery of large or fragile molecules
prerequisites.why: Nanoparticle and liposome systems exist, but delivering enough active compound to dermal fibroblasts without systemic spread is unproven.

prerequisites.tech: Small molecules that selectively reset methylation
prerequisites.why: Current DNMT inhibitors are toxic and non-specific; selective, safe reprogramming molecules are not yet available.
Resetting epigenetic marks risks turning cells cancerous; no long-term human safety data exist.
Regulators have not yet defined how to approve a topical medicine that changes epigenetic age.

pathway.milestone: Laboratory studies reverse epigenetic age in cultured human fibroblasts and in animal skin
pathway.unlocks: proof that the approach is biologically possible.

pathway.milestone: First topical formulations tested in human skin explants and early safety trials
pathway.unlocks: evidence that active molecules can reach target cells safely.

pathway.milestone: Clinical trials measuring skin rejuvenation endpoints such as collagen density and wrinkle depth
Approved therapies for skin aging, and research into applying the same approach to other organs
pathway.unlocks: a new class of medicines that treat aging as a biological process.
